title: Is his music avant garde? Songs as the base
summary: Gil says his music is still song-based and melodic, and discusses the Ampex album.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: You seem to have moved into what one might I suppose call avant garde music at this point as opposed to some of your earlier things. I'm wondering?
I don't know. It's still the same in a way. It's still the, melodic and it's still ........... It doesn't seem avant garde to me at all. (LAUGHTER).
So you think that's because you're, I mean lately because you're in front. (LAUGHTER).
I don't know. Willard Alexander said that too. He thought I was very avant garde. I was surprised. It's only avant garde compared to compared to some other bands maybe that don't, play from
If you listen or if you try to sonerities, to make some assessment of the texture and so forth, I think the feeling is almost inescapable that that's what it is.
And I think the extreme freedom that in certain numbers your performers have, your players, your musicians have is kind of a free flowing thing.

It is. Most all of everything we play is based on a song, it's all a song. I mean the old fashioned symphony in a way. We play mostly songs you know. And to go on and just not play anthing but sounds. Well sometimes it happens accidentally. For example, the Ampex album which wasn't set up and mixed right and then placed right. The first number should not have been the first number and is not mixed right. But, after the first number, most of those are all, well they don't seem avant garde (avon garde?) to me really.

They seem like, well they're modern, they're avant garde modern. They are not (avon garde?), they are modern, in a sense. You know, like some compositions are unusual melodically but nevertheless, they have a definite tune.
